text:
Porter Martone arrived in Philadelphia late last season and put up 10 points in nine games, which set a bar a 20-year-old's first full season was never likely to clear. Through 23 games he has nine points, and none of his last ten games have included a goal. Broad Street Hockey is already writing about what he needs to save his Calder Trophy hopes.

Our numbers see a rookie who is fine, not failing. Forwards picked fourth to eighth since 2005 scored a median 0.44 points a game in their first full season; he's at 0.39. The Flyers do better at five on five with him on the ice than without him, and his 38 hits say he isn't shy about the heavier parts of the game. The cold stretch is some of each: slightly fewer chances, and the ones he gets aren't going in. The change to watch came in Sunday's game, when PHLY Sports' Charlie O'Connor noted Rick Tocchet had swapped Martone and Tyson Foerster on the power play, moving Foerster up to the unit with Matvei Michkov and Trevor Zegras.
